title: Driverless cars and changing cities
text:
This is an outstanding 2-part series of Freakonomics Radio focusing on driverless cars, with a focus on Blue cities (Boston), and the challenges of job losses and politics surrounding this. The discussion can easily be extrapolated to many other areas related to AI.  

It is notable that Uber (and Lyft) have upended the traditional taxi business. And autonomous cars (robot-taxis, Waymos) are doing so to uber driver cars (esp., in red cities) and likely to long haul trucks.  The compelling argument in favor of the technology is safety (most data suggests an overall reduction in crashes and deaths), and flexibility for a variety of niche situations (i.e. disabled communities, etc.). The regressive forces putting the brakes are the unions (teamsters) and their liberal political supporters.  

The very concept of individual car ownership will be challenged by autonomous vehicles. A typical owned car sits idle 96% of the time. The economics for a ride sharing, on-demand autonomous vehicle is compelling in the long term on many levels for most people.

This segment thoughtfully explores this dynamic and concludes there are creative solutions to ease the inexorable future and buffer the inevitable job losses.
